title: Smart client hints and idempotency guardrails for metering
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: At-least-once ingestion, client retries, and network timeouts continue to cause duplicate billable events in edge/ingest paths. Existing approaches (opaque replay tokens, global nonces, and long-lived leases) reduce duplicates but introduce client complexity, backend churn, or contention under high retry rates. This ticket proposes a pragmatic, backwards-compatible server-side guardrail: smart client hints + optimistic reservation and delayed-claim protocol.

Goals: Reduce duplicate charge rate by >=95% for common retry patterns while keeping client changes minimal; avoid long global locks; preserve low-latency happy-path; provide deterministic reconciliation for disputed charges; remain compatible with Dedicated/Private deploy modes.

Proposal summary: 1) Accept optional client-supplied headers (X-Redwood-Idempotency, X-Redwood-Client-TS, X-Redwood-Estimate-Tokens, X-Redwood-Hint-Sig) as hints that enable an optimistic reservation of 'meter credit' at ingest. 2) Create a small, hot idempotency table: per-customer, sharded, in-memory store with tombstone/TTL semantics to track tentative reservations (status=tentative, finalized, cancelled). 3) Reservation window: when a request with a valid idempotency key arrives, the system creates a tentative reservation for estimated tokens and returns an initial ack; the client can finish the request lifecycle (stream commit or finalization) which flips the tentative to committed. If a duplicate retry arrives with the same idempotency key within the reservation window, server returns cached result or reuses the reservation instead of charging again. 4) For clients that don't provide idempotency key, infer lightweight fingerprints (client-ip, immediate payload hash, client-ts) subject to privacy rules as a best-effort dedupe, but always conservative (favor avoiding undercharging). 5) Introduce a delayed-claim reconciliation for edge cases: if multiple tentative reservations exist (e.g., due to clock skew or concurrent clients), run a deterministic tie-breaker based on earliest client-ts + server-received_ts + signature validation. A reconciliation sweep marks duplicates as refunded/resolved and emits accounting events for downstream billing correction.

Design decisions & trade-offs: - We keep reservation TTL short (default 3 minutes) to limit memory pressure and reduce long-lived locks, but allow configurable policy per-customer (enterprise Dedicated might extend). - We bias towards not double-charging in the common case; however if hints are missing and inference result is non-deterministic downstream (e.g., streaming partial), we accept a small residual duplicate rate and rely on reconciliation. - We require optional Hint-Sig when client-provided timestamps are used for tie-breaks to prevent client-crafted replay attacks; signature can be HMAC with customer key (rotate via KMS). For public hosted-tier free accounts the signature is optional. - Privacy: fingerprinting uses hashed salts and is opt-in by customer policy; no raw IPs are stored long-term.

Data model (high-level text): Each idempotency entry = [customer_id, idempotency_key or inferred_fingerprint, status, tentative_tokens, committed_tokens, created_at, last_seen_at, hint_client_ts, hint_sig, origin_edge]. Stored in hot cache (memtable) sharded by customer_id with TTL and backed to cheaper storage for audits.

Rate limiting interaction: Reservations should integrate with our quota counters as provisional reservations to prevent a client from consuming unbounded concurrency tokens during retries. When tentative is created, decrement provisional quota. If finalization fails, provisional quota returns to pool after TTL expiry. This prevents spikes from transient retries.

API/SDK changes: Document new optional headers: X-Redwood-Idempotency (string, UUID recommended), X-Redwood-Client-TS (ISO8601), X-Redwood-Estimate-Tokens (integer), X-Redwood-Hint-Sig (base64 HMAC). SDKs will expose a small helper to generate idempotency keys and attach signatures when customer API key is available. We will provide server-side defaults to avoid breaking existing clients.

Monitoring & metrics: Track metrics per-customer: tentative_reservations, tentative_to_commit_ratio, duplicate_retries_detected, duplicate_charge_rate, reconciliation_refunds_count, reservation_memory_bytes. New alert: duplicate_charge_rate > 0.5% sustained for 30m triggers PagerDuty. Provide console dashboard: per-route duplicate risk and estimated monthly leakage.

Testing & rollout plan: - Unit & integration tests for idempotency table, concurrent reservation attempts, tie-breaker logic, and rate limiter interaction. - Load test simulating clients with high retry rates and clock skew. - Canary rollout: enable for 5% of accounts (beta) -> monitor duplicates and false-positives -> expand. - Migration: existing customers who prefer current behaviour can opt-out per-customer via flag in control plane.

Acceptance criteria: - Server honors X-Redwood-Idempotency for identical keys and prevents double charge for same request in >=95% of retry cases under test harness. - No regressions in median p99 latency for happy-path requests (<= +10ms). - Reconciliation job identifies duplicates and emits correct refund accounting events for at least 99% of synthetic duplicates. - SDK helper and docs published; security review completed.
acceptance_criteria: Idempotency header prevents duplicate billing for identical keys in >=95% retry scenarios under load test
Reservation TTL defaulted to 3m and configurable per-customer; no memory leaks in 48h soak
Reconciliation sweep produces refunds and accounting events for duplicates with <1% false positives in test corpus
Integration test with quota system shows provisional reservations prevent quota exhaustion from rapid retries
Documentation and SDK helper published; security review signed off
comments: 2026-02-22 Maya Chen: initial draft posted to Confluence, flagged for security review. Key open question: default TTL and whether to make signature mandatory for enterprise only.

2026-02-25 Arjun Patel: implemented prototype of hot idempotency table using sharded in-memory store; local load tests look promising. Observed ~92% dedupe rate without signatures when client clock skew is <=2s.

2026-03-01 Security SME (Lena Ortiz): approved HMAC signing approach for Dedicated and Private; recommended using KMS key per-customer and rotating every 90 days. Suggested threat modelling for replay via clock manipulation.
2026-03-05 Product review (Omar Ruiz): requested conservative default (signature optional) to avoid increasing integration friction; agreed to opt-in strict mode for enterprise customers.
2026-03-10 QA (Priya Singh): found edge case where streaming aborts create tentative reservations without commit; added task to emit final 'aborted' event and fast-cancel provisional quota.
2026-03-14 Arjun Patel: canary ready; creating rollout feature flag and canary cohort. Monitoring queries and dashboards in Console PR linked.
